story_description: Provide developers with contextual assistance during hook configuration, including environment variable references, validation feedback, best practices guidance, and interactive testing capabilities to reduce errors and improve hook authoring productivity.
task_description: Create the HookEnvReferenceView SwiftUI component that displays a collapsible panel showing all available Claude Code environment variables (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE) with descriptions, usage examples, availability per event type, and copy-to-clipboard buttons for each variable.
atom_description: Implement the HookEnvReferenceView SwiftUI view that renders a collapsible disclosure group containing a reference table of all Claude Code hook environment variables. Each variable row displays: variable name in monospace font, description text, example value, availability tags indicating which hook events can access it, a critical badge for must-use variables, and a copy button that copies the variable reference (e.g., ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}) to the system pasteboard with visual feedback. The panel also includes a Best Practices section with actionable guidance for using environment variables in hook scripts.
problem_statement: Developers creating hook scripts need quick access to available environment variables without leaving the hook builder interface. Currently they must consult external documentation or guess variable names, leading to typos, using unavailable variables in wrong event contexts, and missing best practices like quoting or portable path patterns. An integrated reference panel directly in the hook configuration UI eliminates context switching and provides copy-to-clipboard convenience, reducing errors and improving hook authoring speed.

CLAUDE_ENV_FILE is only available in SessionStart event type; others available in all events
NSPasteboard is available on macOS for clipboard operations
UserDefaults can store the collapsed/expanded state preference
The panel will be embedded within the hook inspector or builder sidebar
Best practices content is static and does not require dynamic updates
constraints: Must use SwiftUI DisclosureGroup for native collapsible behavior
Variable names must be displayed in monospace font for clarity
Copy button must provide visual feedback within 100ms of tap
Panel width constrained to fit within hook inspector sidebar (max 320pt)
Must not display actual environment variable values from current system (privacy concern)
Must use SF Symbols for icons (copy, checkmark, info) for consistency with macOS design language

edge_cases: Edge case 1: UserDefaults corrupted or inaccessible - default to expanded state and continue without persistence
Edge case 2: NSPasteboard.general.setString fails - log warning, do not show confirmation animation, fail silently
Edge case 3: Very long example value that would overflow - text truncates with ellipsis at row boundary
Edge case 4: User taps copy rapidly multiple times - debounce to prevent clipboard spam, each tap resets 1.5s timer
Edge case 5: System in reduced motion mode - skip animation, show checkmark immediately then reset after 1.5s
Edge case 6: VoiceOver active - announce 'Copied' when copy succeeds in addition to visual feedback
Edge case 7: Extremely large Dynamic Type size - variable rows wrap gracefully, copy button remains accessible
Edge case 8: Panel embedded in narrow container less than 200pt - compact layout stacks elements vertically
Edge case 9: Disclosure group expanded but scrolled out of view - state persists correctly when scrolled back
Edge case 10: Dark mode with high contrast enabled - ensure sufficient contrast ratios for all text and badges
failure_modes: FM1: NSPasteboard access denied by sandbox - log error, show alert 'Unable to copy to clipboard', no crash
FM2: UserDefaults write fails - continue with in-memory state only, log warning, no user-visible impact
FM3: Timer for copy confirmation never fires (rare scheduling issue) - stuck in confirmed state until next interaction, not blocking
FM4: Memory pressure during render - panel may render slowly but will complete, no data loss
FM5: Accessibility API unavailable - labels silently ignored, visual UI works normally
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/HookEnvReferenceView.swift. Remove any references to HookEnvReferenceView from parent views (HookInspectorView or AdvancedHookBuilderView). The hook builder continues to function without the reference panel - users consult external documentation instead. Remove UserDefaults key 'hookEnvReferencePanelExpanded' cleanup is optional. No data migration required.

risks: Risk 1: Clipboard access may be restricted in future macOS versions requiring additional entitlements
Risk 2: Best Practices content may become outdated if Claude Code hooks documentation changes
Risk 3: Additional environment variables may be added by Claude Code requiring panel updates
Risk 4: UserDefaults persistence may conflict with other settings if key name collides
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Use standard NSPasteboard APIs that have stable sandbox permissions; add clipboard entitlement to app if needed
Mitigation 2: Document Best Practices source in code comments; add periodic review reminder in project maintenance docs
Mitigation 3: Design EnvVariableRegistry as easily extensible array; adding new variables requires only adding to the list
Mitigation 4: Use namespaced key 'com.blaze.hookEnvReferencePanelExpanded' to prevent collisions
risk_register.blast_radius: Very low - this is an informational reference panel only. Failure or removal does not affect hook execution or configuration. Users would need to consult external documentation instead, which is the current state before this feature exists.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If clipboard operations prove problematic, remove copy buttons and display variable names as selectable text that users can manually copy. If the entire panel is problematic, remove HookEnvReferenceView and add a link to external Claude Code hooks documentation instead.
